learningObjectives: Explain circumstance rules in a scenario.
Explain single-variable circumstancing in a scenario.
Explain multi-variant circumstancing in a scenario.

elements.description: Keep normal behavior in a base Rule and implement focused exceptions as variants. Rule resolution chooses the applicable behavior without duplicating the whole Process. Use this when the same Rule purpose needs situational differences.

elements.text: Worked example: A shipping policy needs one exception for a particular service tier. Specialize the policy Rule instead of copying every shipping Step.

elements.description: Choose by the requirement: one property → single-variable; a combination → multi-variant; a Case date → date-property; today’s date/time → as-of. If no eligible variant matches, normal behavior comes from the base Rule.

elements.text: Worked example: Choose the clock: an old claim may follow its incident date even today; a seasonal offer follows today’s date.

elements.description: Specify a property and matching value for one-variable exceptions. A date property evaluates Case data; as-of evaluates system time. A higher accessible Rule marked Base resets earlier instances in the same major with lower minor/patch versions. Withdrawing a circumstanced instance removes that variant, not every sibling. Inspect variants in Application Explorer or the Rule header.

elements.text: Worked example: To retire one region’s exception, withdraw that variant and test the remaining base. To reset earlier specializations, review the later Base flag and its version scope.

elements.description: The template declares the properties to evaluate; a definition supplies conditions for their values. Attach the template/definition to a specialized Rule. A template alone does not provide the exception’s matching values. Test matching and nonmatching combinations.

elements.text: Worked example: Template: Region and EmploymentType. Definition: Region=NL and EmploymentType=Contractor. A separate definition supplies another exception; unmatched combinations use the base.

elements.title: Close the notes and explain

examPitfalls.title: Which clock?
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A Case date and the current system date are interchangeable.

examPitfalls.title: Template vs definition
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The template alone specifies the exception values.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Template declares properties; definition supplies conditions.

examPitfalls.title: Variant withdrawal
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Withdrawing one variant suppresses every sibling.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Evaluate remaining instances and distinguish unqualified withdrawal.

quickRecap.value: Base covers normal behavior; eligible matching variants specialize it.
Case date property for historical Case facts; as-of for system time.
